rationale: Agree with the AI, including Critical. Nine wrong passwords at machine cadence from a bulletproof host with a malicious reputation, then a success from the same IP 30 seconds later: the password was guessed. The open question is MFA. The success row does not say whether push was satisfied, so assume the attacker has a session. She is the finance director at a CUI contractor, which makes her mailbox a payment-fraud target as well as a data target.

ai_actions.reason: Kill whatever session the 13:03:10Z sign-in produced.
Hosting provider with a malicious reputation, not residential space. No business traffic will come from it, so the block has no collateral.
Until the sign-in logs show how MFA was satisfied, her registered methods cannot be trusted.
Confirm by phone, not email, since the mailbox may be in the attacker's hands.

added_actions.reason: Hold the account disabled until she is reached by phone and the reset is done with her. Revoking sessions does not stop a fresh sign-in with a known password in the gap before the reset lands.

tuning_notes: Add AuthenticationRequirement and ConditionalAccessStatus to the output. The analyst should not have to open a second query to learn whether the success was password-only.
